entry.name: detonate
entry.digest: Play a score of note events
entry.description: Provides score playback managed using Max messages. The score may be loaded from a MIDI file, or generated using Max functions. The score is not limited to MIDI notes and values; any information can be stored and played back with detonate.

messages.name: follow
messages.description: Causesto behave like a score reader, comparing incoming pitch information to the events stored in its score. When a key number is received in the 2nd (pitch) inlet, and it is the same as the pitch of the current note in the score,sends out the information recorded for that event--except for the delta time--and then moves ahead to the next note event.

messages.name: followat
messages.digest: Find and start following from a specific event
messages.description: The word, followed by a pitch, a velocity, and a MIDI channel number, causesto look for a note event with those attributes in its stored score. If such a note is found,commences score-following from the next event onward. If not, it simply printsin the Max Console.

messages.name: import
messages.description: Same as.

messages.name: in1
messages.digest: Set key number of a note event
messages.description: In 2nd inlet: The number is treated as the key number (pitch) of the note. If no key number has ever been received,is used by default.

messages.name: in2
messages.digest: Set the velocity value of a note event
messages.description: In 3rd inlet: The velocity of the note. If the velocity is 0--indicating a note-off-- the event will be treated as the end of an earlier note-on the same key, and will determine the duration of that earlier note. If no velocity number has ever been received, it isby default.

messages.name: in3
messages.digest: Set a duration value of a note event
messages.description: In 4th inlet: In lieu of a note-off message, a note duration can be supplied as part of the note-on event. If no duration value has ever been received, and no note-off event is received to end the note, a duration ofmilliseconds is used by default.

messages.name: in4
messages.digest: Set a MIDI channel value of a note event
messages.description: In 5th inlet: The MIDI channel of the note. If no channel has ever been specified, notes are recorded on channel 1.

messages.name: in5
messages.digest: Set the track of an event
messages.description: In 6th inlet: The number of a track on which to record the note event. Overdub recording is not possible with, but each recorded note can be tagged with a track number for storing separate tracks of notes internally. If no track number has ever been received, notes are recorded on track 1.

messages.name: in6
messages.digest: Set an extra value for a note event
messages.description: In 7th inlet: An "extra" number, which can be used for any purpose, attached to the note event. This number can be used to provide an additional event parameter, or to serve as a control value in sync with the note. If no number has ever been received in this inlet, it is recorded asby default.

messages.name: in7
messages.digest: Set a second extra value for a note event
messages.description: In right inlet: A second "extra" number.

messages.name: int
messages.description: After amessage has been received, all numbers received are treated as parameters of a note event.In left inlet: The delta time (delay), in milliseconds, since the previous recorded event. This denotes the "inter-onset interval --the time between the beginnings of notes--which effectively determines the rhythm in which the events are recorded. This need not necessarily be the true time in which they occur;believes any (non-negative) delta time it receives.Whenreceives a number in the left inlet while recording, it treats the number as the inter-onset interval (the time elapsed since the previous event), combines it with the numbers most recently received in the other inlets, and records them together as a note event. As with most Max objects, the numbers received in the other inlets are stored for use in subsequent note events triggered by the receipt of a number in the leftmost inlet.Whenhas received amessage, a subsequent number in the 2nd inlet is treated as the key number (pitch) of a note. If the number is the same as the pitch of the current note in the score (or a nearby note), the information recorded for that note--except for the delta time--is sent out.Whenis neither recording nor following, a number in the left inlet has the same effect as themessage.

messages.name: list
messages.description: The first number in the list is used as the delta time, and the other numbers are treated as if they had been received in the other inlets, respectively from left to right.

messages.name: mute
messages.description: Permits the selective muting of note events that meet specific criteria. The wordmust be followed by an event parameter number, a parameter value, and a value oforsignifying "mute" or "unmute".

messages.name: next
messages.digest: Output an event then move to next
messages.description: Once playback of the score has been started with amessage,sends out the event information (except the delta time) for the current note in the score, then sends out the delta time for the next note. That delta time can in turn be used as a delay time before sending anothermessage to detonate. Whenis received on the last note of the score, there is no note following that one, so a unique value ofis sent out the left outlet to signal the end of the score. If amessage is received while the score is not being played back,simply prints the messagein the Max Console.

messages.name: nth
messages.digest: Output note event data for a specified number
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sends out the note information of the event in the score indicated by the number. (Events are numbered beginning with 0.) In place of the delta time for the event, the (cumulative) starting time of the event is sent out the left outlet.

messages.name: open
messages.description: See themessage.

messages.name: params
messages.description: The word, followed by three numbers, modifies the score-following behavior offor cases when the received pitch does not match the pitch of the current note in the score. The first number tellshow many errors to tolerate before moving ahead in the score. The second number tells how many milliseconds to move ahead in the score when too many errors have occurred. The third number, if non-zero, tellsto treat a received pitch that is an octave too high or too low as if it were a match. For example, the messagemeans to allow three successive errors (with octave displacements considered to be a match) before moving ahead one second in the score and resuming. By default,allows 2 errors before moving ahead 200 milliseconds, and does not consider octave pitch displacements to be a match for the stored note.

messages.name: read
messages.description: The wordby itself opens a dialog for loading in a standard MIDI file as contents of thescore. Ifis followed by the name of a MIDI file in Max's search path, that file is read in directly without opening a dialog box. Themessage can also be followed by a number which--if non-zero--causes the time values in the file to be interpreted as milliseconds rather than as bars, beats and ticks at a certain tempo. If the number is 0 or not present, the times are read as bars and beats.

messages.name: record
messages.description: In left inlet: Begins recording numbers coming in the inlets, treating them as parameters of note events to be recorded. The onset of an event is recorded each time a number is received in the left inlet.

messages.name: restore
messages.description: Same as.

messages.name: setparam
messages.description: The messagefollowed by nine list elements will set the parameters of the object much like entering the information into the object's inspector. The first element in the list is a number and signifies which parameter to edit. The remaining elements are the desired settings listed, from left to right, as the "parameter name", the "display mode", the "minimum value", the "maximum value", the "default value", the "graph interval", the "default scaling", and the "Display MIDI note number" flag.
messages.argPattern: parameter:number, name:symbol, display-mode:int, minimum:int, maximum:int, default:int, interval:int, scaling:int, note-number:int

messages.name: start
messages.description: Begins playing back the score, by simply sending out the first delta time. Once playback of the score has been started,messages can be used to send out the next event information.

messages.name: startat
messages.digest: Find and start playback from a specific event
messages.description: The word, followed by a pitch, a velocity, and a MIDI channel number, causesto look for a note event with those attributes in its stored score. If such a note is found,sends out the delta time of the next event, and a subsequentmessage will refer to that next event. If no such note is found,simply printsin the Max Console.

messages.name: stop
messages.description: Stopsfrom recording, playing, or following. It is not necessary to stop detonate before switching directly between,, and.

messages.name: unmute
messages.description: The word, followed by an event parameter number and a parameter value, undoes an earlierof the same criterion. For example,has the same meaning as.

messages.name: unmuteall
messages.description: Undoes the effects of all previousmessages.

messages.name: wclose
messages.description: Closes a previously opened editing window.

messages.name: write
messages.digest: Write a Standard MIDI File to disk
messages.description: Opens a dialog for saving the contents ofas a standard MIDI file. The wordmay optionally be followed by up to two numbers. If the first number is non-zero, the file will be saved with time represented in milliseconds rather than as bars, beats, and ticks in a certain tempo. If the number is 0 or not present, the file is saved as beats. The second number indicates the MIDI file format: 0 (all notes on a single track) o multi-track format, using the track parameter to separate the notes). The contents ofare also saved as part of the patch, when the patch is saved.

messages.name: writemax
messages.digest: Write a Max text file to disk
messages.description: The messagefollowed by a symbol, saves the patch as a Max text file named after the symbol.
